transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
Mostly I’m here because I’m not sleeping right anymore. I’ll lie there a long time, and when I do sleep, I wake up from bad dreams or just little noises. Then I can’t seem to settle back down.
Have you been feeling more anxious or stressed than usual lately?

Yes, I think so. When I go places now, I’m always looking around first—like what might fall, where the exits are, if the floor or the steps look steady. I don’t really sit easy until I’ve checked all that.
Are there any places or situations that you've been avoiding lately?

Yeah… I guess I have. I keep making excuses not to go over to the senior center. And at home, I don’t like working around the garage much anymore, especially by the tools and where I used to keep that ladder. I’ll tell myself I’ll do it later, but mostly I just don’t go near it.
Do you find yourself having repetitive thoughts that you can't seem to get out of your head?

Yes… sometimes. Like if I hear metal scraping, or I see a ladder leaning in someone’s yard, it all just comes back into my head. Feels like I’m right back under there again, waiting for somebody to help me.
Do you feel like you have to do certain things over and over to feel okay or to prevent something bad from happening?
I don’t think so. I mean, I check things sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I have to do something over and over like that. I haven’t really noticed anything like that.
Did something specific happen that's causing these thoughts and feelings to come back into your head?

Yeah… it seems tied to that. When I hear metal scraping, or even just see a ladder leaning somewhere, it comes right back. For a second it’s like I’m under there again, waiting for somebody to come help me.
Can you tell me what happened when you were under something and had to wait for help?

I remember helping with the decorations, and then I remember people talking to me after it happened. But the part where I hit the ground… that’s just gone. It’s like somebody cut that piece out, and I can’t bring it back.
What were you doing when you got hurt under something?

I was helping put up decorations. That much I remember. Then there’s this blank part… I don’t remember the actual fall or hitting the ground. Next thing I can really recall is people there talking to me afterward.
Do you find yourself trying to avoid thinking about what happened when you fell?

Yeah… I do. I’ll tell myself I’m too tired or I’ve got something else to do, but really I just don’t want to go near the senior center or mess around in the garage, especially by the tools or where I used to keep that ladder. It just gets me thinking about it, and I’d rather stay away.
Do you ever feel like you're reliving the moment when you fell, like it's happening all over again?

Sometimes, yeah. Like if I hear metal scraping, or I see a ladder leaning in somebody’s yard, it just jumps back in my head. For a minute it feels like I’m under there again, waiting for somebody to help me.
Do you often feel jittery or on edge, even when there's no apparent reason to be?

Yeah, I guess I do. When I go somewhere now, I’m always looking around first… like what could fall, where the exits are, whether the floor or the steps seem steady. I don’t really settle down until I’ve checked things out a bit.
How long have you been experiencing these anxiety and sleep issues?
It’s been since the ladder accident… about a year and seven months now, I’d say.
Do you ever have moments where you feel like you're actually back at the scene of the ladder accident, reliving it as if it's happening again?

Yeah… sometimes. Like I said, if I hear metal scraping or see a ladder leaning somewhere, it can all come rushing back. For a bit it feels like I’m right there under it again, just waiting for somebody to come help me.
Do you ever have moments where you feel like you're actually back at the scene of the accident, but without any triggers like noises or sights?

Not really without something setting it off, I don’t think. It’s more when I hear metal scrape or see a ladder leaning somewhere… then it jumps right back in my head, like I’m under there again waiting for help.
Do you ever feel like you're back at the scene of the ladder accident without anything specifically reminding you of it?

No… not really out of nowhere. It’s usually something that reminds me, like metal scraping or seeing a ladder leaning in somebody’s yard. Then it kind of jumps back in my head, like I’m under there again waiting for help.
Do you ever find yourself reliving the ladder accident without any reminders, like you're actually back there again?
Not really without something reminding me. It’s more like if I hear metal scrape, or I see a ladder leaning in somebody’s yard, then it comes back hard… like I’m under there again, waiting for help.
